newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank hopes its move will calm mkt.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank hopes its move will calm mkt.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Friday its latest move raising its interest rate should calm the market, but warned that it may take more drastic steps if peso speculation does not die down.
The peso has been hit by speculation arising from the problems of the Thai baht.
"We're not saying this is our last move. Hopefully, this will calm the market," he said.

The Philippine Central Bank started offering three-day reverse repos at 20 percent on Friday, which effectively raises the overnight borrowing rate to 20 from 13 percent, Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters.
Edeza added the overnight lending rate is also being lifted simulatenously to 21 from 14 percent.
In two days, the Central Bank had increased its overnight borrowing rate by a total of 8.75 percentage points to protect the peso.
Traders said the overnight rates are now the highest since March 1995 when they rose to 30 percent as the government defended the peso following the Mexican economic crisis.
